statement: The Taylor series of a function f at a point a is the infinite sum f(x) = sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_n (x-a)^n, where the terms c_n are expressed in terms of the derivatives of f at the single point a (c_n involves f^{(n)}(a)). When a = 0, this is called the Maclaurin series. The partial sum of the first n+1 terms is the nth Taylor polynomial, a degree-n polynomial approximation to f.

symbols.meaning: the single point at which derivatives are evaluated (expansion point)
coefficient of the nth term, expressed via the derivatives of f at a
term/derivative order; the nth Taylor polynomial is the degree-n partial sum

properties.property: The nth Taylor polynomial (partial sum of the first n+1 terms) is a degree-n polynomial approximation of f, and these approximations become generally more accurate as n increases.
properties.why: Taylor polynomials are defined as truncations of the Taylor series

properties.property: Taylor's theorem gives quantitative estimates on the error introduced by truncating to a Taylor polynomial.
properties.why: stated directly as the purpose of Taylor's theorem

properties.property: If the Taylor series converges, its sum is the limit of the sequence of Taylor polynomials; however, a function may differ from the sum of its own convergent Taylor series.
properties.why: convergence of the series does not by itself guarantee equality with f

properties.property: f is analytic at x if it equals the sum of its Taylor series on some open interval (or open disk, in the complex case) containing x; this implies f is analytic at every point of that interval/disk.
properties.why: definition of analyticity in terms of the Taylor series

properties.property: Within its region of convergence, a Taylor/power series sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_n(x-a)^n can be differentiated term by term, d/dx sum c_n(x-a)^n = sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n c_n (x-a)^{n-1}, and integrated term by term, giving C + sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_n/(n+1) (x-a)^{n+1}; the differentiated and integrated series share the original series' radius of convergence (boundary behavior may differ).
properties.why: termwise differentiation/integration is valid inside the radius of convergence

properties.property: A Maclaurin series is the special case of a Taylor series taken at a = 0.
properties.why: definition given for the named special case

assumptions.assumption: f possesses derivatives of all orders at a, so every coefficient c_n is defined.
assumptions.breaks_when: f fails to be infinitely differentiable at a

assumptions.assumption: x lies within the series' region/radius of convergence when using the sum, or its termwise-differentiated/integrated forms.
assumptions.breaks_when: |x-a| exceeds the radius of convergence, or x sits on the boundary where behavior can differ

failure_modes.mode: Series converges but not to f
failure_modes.signature: the Taylor series is convergent at x yet its sum does not equal f(x)
failure_modes.cause: f is not analytic at a even though it is infinitely differentiable there (stated directly in the source as a possibility)

failure_modes.mode: Divergence or altered behavior outside the radius of convergence
failure_modes.signature: partial sums fail to approach f(x), or termwise differentiated/integrated series behave differently at the boundary
failure_modes.cause: x lies outside (or on the boundary of) the radius of convergence shared by the series and its term-by-term derivative/integral

instantiation.why_here: In this project, the ekf_global and ekf_local nodes use an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) from robot_localization to fuse odometry and IMU data into consistent state estimates. The EKF algorithm relies on a first-order Taylor expansion to linearize non-linear process and measurement models around the current state estimate. The listed components depend on this mathematical result purely through the EKF algorithm itself, rather than through direct parameter configuration.

concrete.in_your_project: The non-linear motion or measurement model mapping the robot's state to predicted states or expected sensor observations.
The operating point or current 15-dimensional state estimate (pose, velocities, accelerations) at which partial derivatives are evaluated.
The true or perturbed 15-dimensional robot state vector being estimated.
The expansion coefficients evaluated at a, where c_0 is the function value f(a) and c_1 corresponds to the first-order partial derivatives forming the Jacobian matrix.
The derivative and polynomial order, which is fixed to n = 1 in the Extended Kalman Filter's first-order linearization.
